topic: What if you fell through a tunnel through the Earth
hook: Jump into a hole straight through the Earth.
visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field, deep dark rock lit by a glowing molten orange core, cool blue daylight above
world: A thought experiment today: a perfectly straight tunnel bored through the whole Earth, lit from below by its glowing core
through_line: the jumper's fall, from a green meadow down through the core and out the far side

cast.Jumper: a man in his 30s in a white flight suit and a white helmet with a clear visor, black gloves

props.Earth cutaway: the Earth sliced in half: thin rocky crust, a thick orange mantle, a glowing yellow-white core, one thin straight tunnel through the middle

places.Meadow hole: a perfectly round hole in a green meadow at sunrise, a low grey concrete rim, darkness inside
places.Tunnel: a perfectly round tunnel with smooth dark rock walls dropping straight down, a faint orange glow far below
places.Desert hole: a perfectly round hole in red desert sand under a hard blue midday sky, a low grey concrete rim

cta: Follow for more what-ifs that sound impossible.

captions.hook_line: Jump into a tunnel through the Earth and you'd fall for about 38 minutes, then this happens 🌍
captions.body: A classic physics thought experiment: in a straight airless tunnel through Earth's center, you would speed up all the way to the core, slow down all the way out, stop at the far surface and fall back again. With Earth's real density, the one-way trip takes about 38 minutes, not the 42 a uniform planet would give. It ignores heat, pressure and Earth's spin.
captions.comment_prompt: Would you take the 38-minute trip if it were safe?

youtube_title: Falling Through the Earth Takes 38 Minutes

sources.claim: Straight tunnel through Earth's center: 42 minutes for uniform density, about 38 minutes with Earth's real density structure (Klotz)
Gravity train: oscillation through the Earth, about 42 minutes one way for uniform density
How long it would take to fall through the Earth: 38 minutes 11 seconds

blocks.narration: Jump into a hole straight through the Earth. You would fall for thirty-eight minutes, and then something strange happens.
blocks.visual: The Jumper stepping off the concrete rim of the Meadow hole into the dark round

shots.visual: The Jumper stepping off the concrete rim of the Meadow hole into the dark round opening
The Jumper falling headfirst down the Tunnel, smooth rock walls rushing past, orange glow far below
The Jumper's black gloves spread wide against the rushing dark rock walls of the Tunnel, orange light flickering across them

blocks.narration: Gravity pulls you toward the center, faster and faster. By the center, you are moving several miles every second.
blocks.visual: The Earth cutaway floating in black space, a tiny bright dot sliding down the tu

shots.visual: The Earth cutaway floating in black space, a tiny bright dot sliding down the tunnel toward the glowing core
beats: the dot slides down the tunnel
it speeds up toward the core

shots.visual: The Jumper streaking feet-first through the Tunnel past blinding yellow-white core light
beats: he flashes through the bright light

blocks.narration: But past the center, gravity flips. Now it pulls you backward, slowing you down the whole long way up.
blocks.visual: The Jumper tumbling slowly in the Tunnel, turning from headfirst to feet-first

shots.visual: The Jumper tumbling slowly in the Tunnel, turning from headfirst to feet-first
The Tunnel stretching straight up into darkness toward a tiny circle of blue daylight
The Jumper drifting upward in the Tunnel, slowing, arms spread, cool daylight on his helmet
beats: he rises more and more slowly

blocks.narration: You rise out the other side of the planet, stop exactly at the surface, and hang there for a heartbeat.
blocks.visual: The Jumper rising out of the Desert hole into bright midday sun, red sand all ar

shots.visual: The Jumper rising out of the Desert hole into bright midday sun, red sand all around
beats: his helmet rises out of the hole
he floats up into the sunlight

shots.visual: The Jumper's boots hovering just level with the concrete rim of the Desert hole
beats: his boots slow to a stop

shots.visual: The Jumper floating perfectly still above the Desert hole, arms out, looking around at the desert
beats: he hangs motionless in the air
he glances down at the hole

blocks.narration: Then gravity pulls you back in. With no air to slow you down, you would ride it back and forth forever.
blocks.visual: The Jumper dropping back down into the dark Desert hole

shots.visual: The Jumper dropping back down into the dark Desert hole
The Earth cutaway in black space, a tiny bright dot sliding back and forth through the tunnel, leaving a glowing trail
beats: the dot slides through the core
it swings back the other way

shots.visual: The Jumper rising out of the Meadow hole again at sunrise, then starting to sink back down
